lead: Replit stops working with Anthropic over cost, Apple cracks down on AI nudify apps, and Anthropic reports on AI's effect on its own hiring.

sections.title: Anthropic finance, safety bill and Replit exit
sections.intro: Anthropic's debt talks and lobbying surface alongside Replit dropping it over cost, plus its studies of AI and work.

sections.title: App Store rules, scam defenses and review practice
sections.intro: Apple and Google tighten defenses against abuse, and developers rethink code review for AI-written code.

sections.title: Local LLM speed, measured and estimated
sections.intro: Two Show HN projects and one open-source engine sharpen the picture of running models on your own hardware: Llmspeed estimates per-device speed before you buy, Lithos-metal reports 168 tok/s for Qwen3.8-27B on an M5 Max, and Fakeipedia shows the creative end of local-scale generation.

sections.title: AI funding and enterprise consolidation
sections.intro: A cluster of deals: Scarlet raised $50M to speed up AI medical device certification, Mistlabs took $26M for its ambient assistant Ambi, Reach Security passed $50M for AI-driven exposure management, and Workday agreed to buy identity startup C1.ai. Meanwhile an FT profile floats Alexandr Wang as a potential Zuckerberg successor.

sections.title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash arrives
sections.intro: DeepSeek shipped V4.1 Flash 1017, the first model on its Causal Encoder-Decoder architecture: 552B total parameters, 8B active on input and 16B on output, native image understanding, and KV cache compressed to a quarter of the previous Flash generation.

sections.title: Surveillance, from ad-tech spyware to license plate readers
sections.intro: Two accountability stories: Citizen Lab shows an Israeli spyware firm used the major ad platforms as a zero-click malware delivery pipe, and Benn Jordan explains to The Verge how the anti-Flock backlash went from YouTube investigations to a Senate hearing and cancelled contracts.

sections.title: The money around AI
sections.intro: Bloomberg profiles Blackstone's Jon Gray and his $200B AI data center bet, while the WSJ reports insurers worry AI liability claims could outpace coverage limits.
